title: Practice baseline
disclaimer: This pack is NOT law anywhere. It collects checks that hold in most codes, so that a plan in a jurisdiction codraft has not encoded still gets looked at rather than passed in silence. A clean result here says the plan is not obviously broken. It says nothing whatever about compliance.

design.$note: Targets the SOLVER aims at, so a plan is drawn trying to meet these rather than drawn freely and failed against them afterwards. They repeat the figures asserted by baseline.habitable.width and baseline.habitable.area below; tests/test_baseline_targets.py fails if the two ever drift apart.

rules.title: Every room can be walked out of
rules.message: {name} has no route to any exit. Nothing else in this report matters until that is fixed.
rules.note: This is geometry, not code: a room with no door onto a route reaching an exterior door or a stair is unusable everywhere.

rules.title: Habitable rooms have a window
rules.message: {name} is a habitable room with no window.
rules.note: Nearly every code requires daylight and natural ventilation to habitable rooms, though the area differs.

rules.title: Glazing area against floor area
rules.message: {name} has glazing of {glazing_ratio} of its floor area; 8% is a common floor.
rules.note: 8% is at the lenient end. Local requirements run from about 8% to 20%.

rules.title: Habitable rooms are large enough to use
rules.message: {name} is {area_m2} m². Codes commonly set a floor between 6.5 and 9.5 m².

rules.title: Habitable rooms are wide enough to use
rules.message: {name} is {width_mm} mm across at its narrowest.

rules.title: Clear ceiling height
rules.message: {name} has about {clear_height_mm} mm clear to the ceiling.
rules.note: Depends on the assumed slab and finish thickness; confirm against a section.

rules.title: Corridors are wide enough to pass along
Doorways are wide enough to pass through
rules.message: A doorway serving {serves} gives {clear_width_mm} mm clear.

rules.title: The building has a way out
rules.message: The building has no exit door onto the outside.

rules.title: Stairs are not too steep
rules.message: A stair rises at {pitch_degrees}°, on a {riser_mm} mm riser and a {going_mm} mm going.
rules.note: 42° is the limit for a private stair in several codes; public stairs are held to less.

rules.title: Riser and going are in proportion
rules.message: Twice the riser plus the going is {two_r_plus_g} mm; a comfortable stair falls between 550 and 700 mm.
rules.note: The Blondel relation, which appears in codes worldwide in one form or another.

rules.title: Headroom over the stair
rules.message: Headroom over the stair is {headroom_mm} mm.
